contents.description: Massed levies who loose arrows by the bucket and hope some land.
A mob with pitchforks, torches and strong opinions.
A shambling multitude that wins by simply being too many.
Trained bowmen who shoot straight and keep their distance.
Nimble foot who fight in loose order from cover.
Loose-order spearmen, quick on their feet and on rough ground.
Plunderers who hit hard, grab what they can and run.
Scouts and slingers who pester and are gone before the charge lands.
Wild warriors who charge in a howling rush.
Engines that hurl bolts, stones or worse.
Veteran foot, the finest blades in the host.
Armoured foot who hold their ground with axe and shield.
Crossbows or bows sheltered behind tall shields.
A hedge of long pikes, deadly while it keeps its shape.
A wall of shields and spears, the backbone of many a host.
Armoured carts bristling with shooters.
Fighters without drill, strong in the first clash.
Riders on beasts nobody else would mount.
Mounts that carry foot soldiers to the fight and leave them there.
Chariots that race in, shoot and wheel away.
The best-mounted riders, fighting in close order.
Riders who shoot from the saddle and never quite close.
Light riders who throw javelins and wheel away.
Armoured riders who charge knee to knee.
Riders armoured head to hoof, mount included.
Great beasts that trample what they cannot frighten.

contents.AC:
Armoured lizards, slow to start and hard to stop.

#### Cost
Each stand carrying a Charging Camelry or Armored Camelry card costs 1 point less.

Charging Camelry and Armored Camelry go on every stand of a troop entry or on none of them.

#### In play
The stands fight as heavy riders but frighten horses.
contents.AM:
Nothing waits quite as patiently as a goblin under a bush.

#### Cost
1 point

#### In play
Up to three stands deploy hidden in rough ground and are revealed when they move or are approached.
contents.CC:
Lizards, but faster and angrier.

#### Cost
Each stand carrying a Charging Camelry or Armored Camelry card costs 1 point less.

Charging Camelry and Armored Camelry go on every stand of a troop entry or on none of them.

#### In play
The stands charge as light riders and frighten horses.
contents.CF:
The lizards do not enjoy it either.

#### Cost
1 point

#### In play
Foot stands shelter behind a line of kneeling beasts.
contents.CH:
Chained so that nobody runs, least of all the thralls.

#### Cost
Nothing

Chained Together goes on every stand of a troop entry or on none of them.

#### In play
The stands may not recoil, and neither may they pursue.
contents.CT:
Knights of the Iron Crown rarely stop to ask.

#### Cost
1 point for each card, never more than 2 points

A Charge Through card covers every stand in its troop entry, never a single stand.

#### In play
A stand that wins its combat may keep going into the next enemy.
contents.DC:
Scarecrows in borrowed helmets.

#### Cost
The card costs 1 point for each stand it may swap or remove:

#### In play
Dummy stands are deployed and revealed, or removed, once the enemy has committed.
contents.DD:
Knights who never did like their horses.

#### Cost
1 point

One card lets every eligible troop entry in the army dismount at deployment.

#### In play
Eligible stands may be deployed on foot as the troop type the list names.
contents.ES:
Painted wicker mammoths, pushed by very brave children.

#### Cost
2 points

The army list says whether an army may raise an Elephant Screen.

An army that buys this card may not field a single elephant stand.

#### In play
Screening stands count as elephants to anything that fears them.
contents.ET:
The other half of the wicker mammoth.

#### Cost
The army list says whether an army may raise an Elephant Screen.

The army list marks the troops that may screen and the troops they screen.

#### In play
Marks the stands an Elephant Screen may stand in front of.
contents.FC:
Palisades of rune-carved oak, ditches seeded with iron caltrops, and a very bad-tempered gatekeeper.

#### Cost
1 point

#### Choosing this card
The army list says whether an army may raise a Fortified Camp.

#### In play
The camp adds +2 to its close combat factor.

Everything else about the camp stays the same:
- The camp may hold a garrison.
- The camp may be plundered.
contents.HD:
Deep ranks of spear-dancers, eight elves deep.

#### Cost
Nothing

#### In play
Two stands may stack one behind the other and fight as one.
contents.HL:
Shieldwalls that sing while they are pushed.

#### Cost
The first Hold the Line card is free; each one after it costs 1 point

A Hold the Line card covers every stand in its troop entry, never a single stand.

#### Choosing this card
No army may buy more than 3 Hold the Line cards.

#### In play
The stands ignore their first recoil each battle.
contents.LC:
Giant lizards, in this part of the world.

#### Cost
Nothing

#### In play
The stands frighten horses and count as rough-going beasts.
contents.MD:
Getting off a mammoth is harder than it looks.

#### Cost
2 points

One card lets every eligible troop entry in the army dismount in the middle of a battle.

#### In play
Eligible stands may dismount once, in their own bound.
contents.MI:
Goblins on borrowed ponies, briefly.

#### Cost
Nothing if the card is bought for one stand.

1 point if the card is bought for two stands or more.

The card may be bought for any number of the stands in a troop entry.

#### In play
The stands ride to battle and march as mounted.
contents.NC:
Some hosts carry everything they own on their backs, and like it that way.

#### Cost
3 points

#### In play
The army deploys without a camp and can never have one plundered.
contents.PD:
Hedge-witches can grow a thorn wall overnight, if paid in honey.

#### Cost
½ point for each card taken

#### In play
Each card places one stretch of stakes, ditch or thorn hedge before deployment.
contents.PL:
Hand-cranked bolt throwers on squeaking wheels.

#### Cost
1 point per stand

#### In play
Each stand drags a light war-cart that shoots as artillery.
contents.PT:
Mammoth calves, goats and one indignant yak.

#### Cost
1 point

#### In play
The camp may be moved once during deployment, and it may not be combined with a Fortified Camp.
contents.SB:
Archers crouched behind a wall of shields, picking their moments.

#### Cost
The card itself costs nothing, but a bowman stand is traded for the support it lends.

#### In play
A bowman stand joins a Supportable stand and lends it shooting.
contents.SC:
Mostly aimed in the right direction.

#### Cost
2 points

#### In play
Once per battle, a stampede is loosed at an enemy stand and is removed after its charge.
contents.SF:
Duellists on horseback, each with a better sword than the last.

#### Cost
The card costs nothing, but each stand carrying it costs 3 ½ points.

Sword-Fighting Cavalry goes on every stand of a troop entry or on none of them.

#### In play
The stands fight mounted enemies at +1 and foot at −1.
contents.SP:
Shields wide enough for two.

#### Cost
The card itself costs nothing, but a bowman stand is traded for the support it lends.

#### In play
Marks the stands that Supporting Bowmen may join.
contents.SS:
Elven archers darken the sky, briefly and politely.

#### Cost
1 point per stand

Shower Shooting goes on every stand of a troop entry or on none of them.

#### In play
The stands shoot at two paces further than their kind.
contents.SV:
Squires with sharpened ladles.

#### Cost
Nothing

Valets always come in pairs of stands.

#### In play
Each knight stand may leave its squires behind as a separate stand.
contents.SW:
The banner has been lost twice and stolen back three times.

#### Cost
Nothing

#### In play
The wagon carries the army’s banner. Stands beside it fight with a +1 while it stands.

contents.ambush:
Goblin sappers wait under the moss until the drums stop.

#### In play
Roll a die at deployment; that many stands may hide in rough ground away from the usual lines.
contents.armored:
Plates hammered from fallen star-iron turn the arrows aside.

#### In play
Enemy shooting at this stand counts one less.
contents.away:
The riders vanish into the cloud bank and come down somewhere else entirely.

#### In play
The stand may leave the table and return on a later turn.
contents.brittle:
Hired sprites who remember an urgent appointment the moment the battle turns.

#### In play
The stand is shattered whenever it is beaten in close combat.
contents.champion:
A duellist who hunts other heroes across the field.

#### In play
The hero fights duels as if it cost three points more.
contents.chargeThrough:
The lancers trust the pikemen to open their files on the horn call.

#### In play
One tactical move may pass through friendly close order foot.
contents.craven:
Mushroom folk who would honestly rather be anywhere else today.

#### In play
The stand never moves into contact and never pursues.
contents.deadly:
Their blades sing a single note that ends conversations.

#### In play
The stand adds one in close combat.
contents.delayedEntry:
The summoning circle is still smoking when the battle starts.

#### In play
Marked stands arrive later, when the army spends five command points.
contents.fast:
Hooves shod with quicksilver carry them before the dust settles.

#### In play
The stand moves a little further than others of its kind.
contents.fierce:
Bog trolls who cannot be talked out of a good brawl.

#### In play
The stand must follow up and may never break off.
contents.flying:
Leathery wings beat over the heads of the battle line.

#### In play
The stand flies, hovering in place or zooming across the table.
contents.fortifiedCamp:
A ring of thorn hedges grown overnight by an irritable druid.

#### In play
The camp fights harder when it is attacked.
contents.hearten:
A banner that hums softly whenever courage is needed.

#### In play
A beaten stand adds one before the result is read.
contents.holdTheLine:
Drilled shieldmaidens who stay put when the foe breaks.

#### In play
Play the card to stop a pursuit after close combat.
contents.illusion:
The wizard's apprentice paints soldiers on the morning fog.

#### In play
A stand on the table is either a phantom or something else in disguise.
contents.marksman:
Owl-eyed bowmen who can split a falling acorn.

#### In play
The stand adds one when it shoots.
contents.massive:
Giants who simply do not get pushed around.

#### In play
The stand is never pushed back and crushes friends who fall back into it.
contents.mindblast:
A whisper that crawls into the ear and curdles the nerve.

#### In play
The stand attacks minds at long range and ignores the terrain between.
contents.mobileInfantry:
Spearmen who ride to the battle on giant tortoises and walk the last mile.

#### In play
Marked stands move quickly until they first fight.
contents.negateMagic:
A silver ward that makes spells slide off like rain on oilcloth.

#### In play
The stand shrugs off magical attacks.
contents.noCamp:
The horde carries everything it owns, which is not much.

#### In play
The army has no camp.
contents.packTrain:
Herds of woolly goats that wander wherever the shepherd sleeps.

#### In play
The camp may stand anywhere along the base edge.
contents.preparedDefenses:
Ditches full of sharpened bones dug the night before.

#### In play
Each card places one obstacle in front of the army.
contents.prowess:
Weapons forged in dragonfire glow along the line.

#### In play
A winning stand adds one before the result is read.
contents.rangedAttack:
Rock-throwing ogres who never learned to use a bow.

#### In play
The stand may shoot even though its kind usually cannot.
contents.regenerate:
Bone soldiers who pull themselves back together after the fight.

#### In play
A lost stand may return by paying command points.
contents.slow:
Clay golems who take their time about everything.

#### In play
The stand moves a little less than others of its kind.
contents.spellblast:
Fireballs, frogs from the sky and other loud arguments.

#### In play
The stand casts a long range attack, limited or unlimited.
contents.spikedCarts:
Wheelbarrows bristling with pitchforks, pushed by stubborn farmers.

#### In play
The stand fights better against riders but moves only a short way.
contents.subcommander:
A sergeant who knows what the general wants before the general does.

#### In play
Moves that include this hero cost fewer command points.
contents.supportingShooters:
A thin line of slingers tucked behind the shield wall.

#### In play
The stand adds one against charging riders and wild warriors.
contents.terrainAffinity:
Swamp lizards who treat the marsh like a paved road.

#### In play
The stand treats two chosen kinds of terrain as open ground.
contents.terror:
A shambling horror whose very shadow makes horses bolt.

#### In play
A beaten enemy panics and a doubled one is destroyed.
contents.unreliable:
Mercenary imps whose loyalty lasts exactly as long as the pay.

#### In play
When the command die rolls a one, the costliest such stand leaves.
contents.unruly:
Undead conscripts who hear orders but rarely listen.

#### In play
The stand costs one more command point to move.
contents.weaken:
Enchanted sleepers still yawning when the trumpets sound.

#### In play
A beaten stand subtracts one before the result is read.

contents.description: Levas en masa que disparan flechas a cubos y esperan que alguna acierte.
Una turba con horcas, antorchas y opiniones firmes.
Una multitud tambaleante que gana por ser demasiados.
Arqueros entrenados que disparan recto y guardan la distancia.
Infantería ágil que combate en orden abierto desde la cobertura.
Lanceros en orden abierto, rápidos en terreno difícil.
Saqueadores que golpean fuerte, cogen lo que pueden y huyen.
Exploradores y honderos que hostigan y desaparecen antes de la carga.
Guerreros salvajes que cargan entre aullidos.
Ingenios que lanzan virotes, piedras o cosas peores.
Infantería veterana, las mejores hojas de la hueste.
Infantería acorazada que aguanta con hacha y escudo.
Ballestas o arcos tras escudos altos.
Un seto de picas largas, letal mientras mantiene la forma.
Un muro de escudos y lanzas, espina dorsal de muchas huestes.
Carros blindados erizados de tiradores.
Combatientes sin instrucción, fuertes en el primer choque.
Jinetes sobre bestias que nadie más montaría.
Monturas que llevan a la infantería al combate y la dejan allí.
Carros que llegan, disparan y dan media vuelta.
Los jinetes mejor montados, en orden cerrado.
Jinetes que disparan desde la silla y nunca llegan a cerrar.
Jinetes ligeros que lanzan jabalinas y se retiran.
Jinetes acorazados que cargan rodilla con rodilla.
Jinetes acorazados de pies a cabeza, montura incluida.
Grandes bestias que pisotean lo que no logran asustar.

Jinetes sobre bestias que nadie más montaría.
Monturas que llevan a la infantería al combate y la dejan allí.
Carros que llegan, disparan y dan media vuelta.
Los jinetes mejor montados, en orden cerrado.
Jinetes que disparan desde la silla y nunca llegan a cerrar.
Jinetes ligeros que lanzan jabalinas y se retiran.
Jinetes acorazados que cargan rodilla con rodilla.
Jinetes acorazados de pies a cabeza, montura incluida.
Grandes bestias que pisotean lo que no logran asustar.

contents.ambush:
Los zapadores trasgos esperan bajo el musgo hasta que callan los tambores.

#### En juego
Tira un dado al desplegar; esa cantidad de peanas puede esconderse en terreno abrupto lejos de las líneas habituales.
contents.armored:
Placas forjadas con hierro de estrella desvían las flechas.

#### En juego
El enemigo que dispara contra esta peana cuenta uno menos.
contents.away:
Los jinetes desaparecen en las nubes y bajan en otro lugar.

#### En juego
La peana puede salir de la mesa y volver en un turno posterior.
contents.brittle:
Duendes a sueldo que recuerdan una cita urgente en cuanto la batalla se tuerce.

#### En juego
La peana queda destrozada siempre que pierde un combate cuerpo a cuerpo.
contents.champion:
Un duelista que caza a otros héroes por el campo.

#### En juego
El héroe libra duelos como si costara tres puntos más.
contents.chargeThrough:
Los lanceros confían en que los piqueros abran filas al toque de cuerno.

#### En juego
Un movimiento táctico puede atravesar infantería amiga en orden cerrado.
contents.craven:
Gente seta que, sinceramente, preferiría estar en cualquier otra parte.

#### En juego
La peana nunca entra en contacto ni persigue.
contents.deadly:
Sus hojas cantan una sola nota que pone fin a las conversaciones.

#### En juego
La peana suma uno en combate cuerpo a cuerpo.
contents.delayedEntry:
El círculo de invocación aún humea cuando empieza la batalla.

#### En juego
Las peanas marcadas llegan más tarde, cuando el ejército gasta cinco puntos de mando.
contents.fast:
Herraduras de azogue los llevan antes de que se asiente el polvo.

#### En juego
La peana mueve algo más que otras de su clase.
contents.fierce:
Trols de ciénaga a los que no se puede disuadir de una buena pelea.

#### En juego
La peana debe avanzar tras vencer y nunca puede retirarse.
contents.flying:
Alas correosas baten sobre la línea de batalla.

#### En juego
La peana vuela, inmóvil en el aire o cruzando la mesa a toda velocidad.
contents.fortifiedCamp:
Un anillo de setos de espinos crecido en una noche por un druida irritable.

#### En juego
El campamento lucha con más fuerza cuando lo atacan.
contents.hearten:
Un estandarte que zumba suavemente cuando hace falta valor.

#### En juego
Una peana vencida suma uno antes de leer el resultado.
contents.holdTheLine:
Escuderas bien instruidas que no se mueven cuando el enemigo huye.

#### En juego
Juega la carta para impedir una persecución tras el combate.
contents.illusion:
El aprendiz del mago pinta soldados en la niebla de la mañana.

#### En juego
Una peana de la mesa es un fantasma u otra cosa disfrazada.
contents.marksman:
Arqueros con ojos de búho capaces de partir una bellota al caer.

#### En juego
La peana suma uno al disparar.
contents.massive:
Gigantes a los que simplemente no se empuja.

#### En juego
La peana nunca retrocede y aplasta a los amigos que retroceden contra ella.
contents.mindblast:
Un susurro que se mete en el oído y cuaja el ánimo.

#### En juego
La peana ataca las mentes a larga distancia e ignora el terreno intermedio.
contents.mobileInfantry:
Lanceros que van a la batalla a lomos de tortugas gigantes y caminan la última milla.

#### En juego
Las peanas marcadas mueven deprisa hasta su primer combate.
contents.negateMagic:
Una guarda de plata que hace resbalar los hechizos como lluvia en hule.

#### En juego
La peana resiste los ataques mágicos.
contents.noCamp:
La horda carga con todo lo que tiene, que no es mucho.

#### En juego
El ejército no tiene campamento.
contents.packTrain:
Rebaños de cabras lanudas que van donde duerma el pastor.

#### En juego
El campamento puede ir en cualquier punto del borde propio.
contents.preparedDefenses:
Zanjas llenas de huesos afilados cavadas la noche anterior.

#### En juego
Cada carta coloca un obstáculo frente al ejército.
contents.prowess:
Armas forjadas en fuego de dragón brillan a lo largo de la línea.

#### En juego
Una peana vencedora suma uno antes de leer el resultado.
contents.rangedAttack:
Ogros que lanzan rocas y nunca aprendieron a usar un arco.

#### En juego
La peana puede disparar aunque los de su clase no suelan hacerlo.
contents.regenerate:
Soldados de hueso que se recomponen después del combate.

#### En juego
Una peana perdida puede volver pagando puntos de mando.
contents.slow:
Gólems de arcilla que se toman su tiempo para todo.

#### En juego
La peana mueve algo menos que otras de su clase.
contents.spellblast:
Bolas de fuego, ranas del cielo y otras discusiones ruidosas.

#### En juego
La peana lanza un ataque a larga distancia, limitado o ilimitado.
contents.spikedCarts:
Carretillas erizadas de horcas empujadas por granjeros tozudos.

#### En juego
La peana lucha mejor contra jinetes pero mueve muy poco.
contents.subcommander:
Un sargento que sabe lo que quiere el general antes que el propio general.

#### En juego
Los movimientos que incluyen a este héroe cuestan menos puntos de mando.
contents.supportingShooters:
Una fina línea de honderos tras el muro de escudos.

#### En juego
La peana suma uno contra jinetes a la carga y guerreros salvajes.
contents.terrainAffinity:
Lagartos de pantano que recorren la ciénaga como si fuera un camino empedrado.

#### En juego
La peana trata dos tipos de terreno elegidos como terreno abierto.
contents.terror:
Un horror tambaleante cuya sombra desboca a los caballos.

#### En juego
Un enemigo vencido entra en pánico y uno doblado es destruido.
contents.unreliable:
Diablillos mercenarios cuya lealtad dura exactamente lo que dura la paga.

#### En juego
Cuando el dado de mando saca un uno, la peana más cara de este tipo se marcha.
contents.unruly:
Reclutas no muertos que oyen las órdenes pero rara vez escuchan.

#### En juego
Mover la peana cuesta un punto de mando más.
contents.weaken:
Durmientes encantados que aún bostezan cuando suenan las trompetas.

#### En juego
Una peana vencida resta uno antes de leer el resultado.
